news.headline: PSX surges over 5,000 points as US-Iran attacks pause and SBP rate-hold expectations lift sentiment
news.summary: Monday session (this checkpoint, from Friday's confirmed close of 171,021.20): Pakistan Observer reported the KSE-100 'gained 5,151 points in early trading session to climb to 176,172.20 points,' a positive change of 3.01 percent, citing Iranian military spokesperson Mohammad Reza Akraminia's statement that the US had suspended its attacks over the past two nights, prompting Iran to halt retaliatory operations, plus market anticipation that the State Bank of Pakistan's Monetary Policy Committee (meeting today, Jul 27) would keep the policy rate unchanged. PakTribune corroborated the same figures. PSX's own official market-summary page (psx.com.pk/market-summary/, captured 2026-07-27 12:25:02 PKT, market status 'Open') showed the index further extending to 176,284.99, up 5,263.79 points (+2.99%), volume 487,218,011 shares across 225,355 trades, breadth 430 advancing vs 56 declining. No SBP MPC decision had been announced as of this checkpoint (11:00-12:25 PKT); a prior Topline Securities poll (already logged Jul 21 and Jul 24) found 97% of respondents expect the rate held at 11.5%. Logged as impact 4 (sharp, market-wide geopolitical-driven move, >3% single-session swing) per desk news-impact criteria (Rule 10); escalation flagged. No individual stock-level figures independently verified in the sources reviewed beyond the index-wide move.

news.headline: SBP keeps policy rate unchanged at 11.5pc - first MPC decision of FY27
news.summary: SBP Governor Jameel Ahmed announced at today's Monetary Policy Committee meeting (first of FY27): 'MPC has decided to keep the policy rate unchanged at 11.5pc,' marking a second consecutive pause (rate was raised 100bps to 11.5% in April 2026, after a 50bps cut to 10.5% in December 2025). Governor cited inflation of 11.1% in June (down from 11.7% in May), noting the earlier declining trend was interrupted by Middle East geopolitical tensions, and expressed hope for further decline within one to two months absent renewed escalation. SBP reiterated targets/guidance: FX reserves target of $20.2bn by December 2026 (vs $18.4bn achieved end-June 2026); current account deficit projected at 0-1% of GDP; remittances target raised to $44bn for the year (from a prior $41.6bn); total external debt servicing of $21.5bn. Decision matched the widely-expected outcome (a Topline Securities poll already logged this newslog, 2026-07-21/07-24, found 97%/over 90% of respondents expected a hold). Logged as impact 4 per desk news-impact criteria (SBP rate decision); escalation flagged.

Buying interest was observed in automobile assemblers, cement, commercial banks, oil & gas exploration companies, OMCs and power generation, with index-heavy stocks OGDC, PPL, POL, MARI, PSO, HUBCO, ARL (Attock Refinery, ATRL), HBL, MCB and MEBL trading in the green. Driver: continuation of the pause in US-Iran fighting (per the Iranian military spokesperson's statement already logged) dragging oil prices lower and easing inflation risk. No confirmed closing-bell figure for the full session found in sources reviewed as of this checkpoint; logged as impact 3 (extension/confirmation of an already-flagged impact-4 macro move, not a new independent driver).

news.headline: KSE-100 confirmed Monday close: index surges over 7,200 points as US-Iran tensions ease and oil prices plunge
news.summary: Confirmed final close, from Friday's 171,021.20: Dawn reported the KSE-100 settled at 178,262.33 points, up 7,241.13 points (+4.23%), intraday peak 178,588.33, article published Jul 27, 2026, updated 04:54pm PKT. PSX's own market-summary page (psx.com.pk/market-summary/, captured 2026-07-27 17:40:01 PKT, market status 'Closed') showed the same 178,262.33 level and +7,241.13-point gain but a +4.06% change (percentage-basis discrepancy between the two sources, both quoted exactly as reported), volume 1,032,191,519 shares, 436,420 trades. Mettis Global's 'PSX Closing Bell: Good Times Roll' (mettisglobal.news/latest, published 04:33pm PKT) corroborated the greater-than-7,200-point surge, attributing it to 'easing geopolitical tensions and a sharp decline in global oil prices.' Drivers per Dawn: hopes for a US-Iran diplomatic resolution and resumption of Strait of Hormuz shipping; Brent crude fell over 7% to briefly dip below $90/barrel, WTI down 4% to $85.45; the State Bank of Pakistan held its policy rate at 11.5% (already logged this cycle). AKD Securities' Awais Ashraf called the SBP decision 'a cautious stance,' while predicting future rate cuts given a 'disinflationary trend, a comfortable external account position, weakening leading economic indicators.' Dawn reported that UBL, FFC, ENGROH, MEBL and LUCK collectively contributed approximately 2,546 points to the day's gain. Logged as impact 4 (sharp market-wide move, single-session index gain over 4%) per desk news-impact criteria (Rule 10); this is the confirmed final close superseding the intraday +5,263.79-point/+2.99% and +6,600.15-point/+3.86% reads already logged earlier this cycle.

news.headline: Kospi triggers circuit breaker (8th this year) as chip-sector selloff drags South Korea, Japan markets down; Samsung, SK Hynix each fall over 7-12%
news.summary: Published Jul 28, 2026: South Korea's Kospi index plunged more than 8% intraday (some reports cite up to 10%), triggering a market-wide circuit breaker for the 8th time this year; Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix each fell roughly 7-12% in various snapshots cited across sources, given their outsized index weight. Driver cited across sources: a contagion effect from the US semiconductor sector (Nvidia weakness/concerns over its financial model) plus the listing of CXMT, China's largest memory-chipmaker, on fears that IPO proceeds would let it accelerate competition with Samsung and SK Hynix in DRAM/HBM memory chips; region-wide selloff also hit Tokyo. No PSX-listed semiconductor constituent exists in the universe and no direct PSX-ticker read-through is confirmed in sources reviewed; logged as a MACRO/global-markets spillover-risk item (foreign-market circuit breaker/tech-sector shock) for context on global risk appetite at this checkpoint, not a PSX-specific event.

news.headline: PTCL Group achieves strong financial results with 62% topline growth YoY - 1HCY26 net profit Rs4.7bn vs H1CY25 net loss Rs9.90bn
news.summary: Published Jul 28, 2026 3:41pm PKT: PTCL Group (PSX: PTC) reported consolidated net profit of Rs4.7 billion for the half year ended June 30, 2026, versus a consolidated net loss of Rs9.90 billion in H1CY25 (per Mettis Global's earlier report 'PTCL loss nears Rs10bn in H1 2025' - the six months ended June 30, 2025 - an 11.06% wider loss than H1CY24's Rs8.91bn) - an earnings-surprise turnaround. Consolidated revenue grew 62% YoY; consolidated operating profit grew 226% YoY, driven by the successful amalgamation of Ufone and Telenor Pakistan under Pak Telecom Mobile Limited (PTML) completed in Q2 2026, plus growth in fixed broadband, enterprise and wholesale segments. No EPS figure disclosed in the source reviewed. Logged as impact 4 (material earnings surprise, loss-to-profit turnaround) per desk news-impact criteria (Rule 10); escalation flagged.

news.headline: PM orders increase in country's strategic petroleum reserves; Cabinet Committee on Energy approves changes to Oil Refining Policy 2023
news.summary: Published/updated Jul 28, 2026 1:36pm PKT: Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, chairing a meeting of the Cabinet Committee on Energy at the PM's House, approved amendments to the 'Pakistan Oil Refining Policy for Upgradation of Existing Brownfield Refineries 2023' - requiring production of environment-friendly Euro-V-standard fuel, reduction of furnace oil and low-quality petroleum products output, and compliance with international environmental commitments. The amendments aim to unlock nearly $6 billion in investment across Pakistan's five existing refineries (combined capacity approx. 449,400 bpd, currently operating at less than half that level) - a follow-through on the Petroleum Division's amendments to the same Brownfield Refining Policy first reported 2026-07-13 (already logged this newslog at impact 4). PM Shehbaz directed authorities to promote the revised policy among Gulf investors via roadshows in Qatar, Saudi Arabia and other Gulf states to attract investment in brownfield refinery upgrade projects, and ordered reforms to the Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (Ogra). No individual refinery (ATRL, NRL, PRL, PARCO, Cnergyico) named specifically in this article; tagged to the universe's core-tier refiners (ATRL, NRL, PRL) as the direct beneficiaries of a sector-wide brownfield-refining policy. Logged as impact 4 (regulatory action) per desk news-impact criteria (Rule 10); escalation flagged.
